page: Amazon Web Services a1.metal is a bare-metal instance powered by a first-generation 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processor. It features 16 physical Cortex-A72 cores running at a fixed clock speed of 2.3 GHz, with single-threaded execution per core and dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of RAM, offering 2.0 GB of memory per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, with no L3 cache present. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps, includes hardware-accelerated AES instruction support, and lacks local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates moderate multi-threaded performance alongside constrained single-core throughput. Stress-ng tests record a single-core score of 1507.99 and a multi-core score of 24102.93, both placing in average ranges. However, single-core Geekbench metrics (418.0) and text processing scores (602.0) fall into lower percentiles. Memory performance shows high cached read bandwidth (572.2 GB/sec), but drops to 34.01 GB/sec for uncached reads and 10.05 GB/sec for uncached writes. Database performance via Redis SET operations reaches 8.6 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 3.68 GB/sec.

The hardware profile provides bare-metal direct access to physical Arm cores without virtualization overhead, offering qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out workloads tailored to Arm architecture. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it suitable for containerized web applications, microservices, light database operations, and software compilation tasks. Workloads dependent on heavy single-threaded computational power, extensive vector instruction sets, high uncached memory write bandwidth, or large-scale LLM inference face notable performance tradeoffs.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.metal is a bare-metal cloud instance equipped with 16 physical 64-bit Arm Cortex-A72 cores operating at 2.3 GHz and 32.0 GB of RAM, delivering a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Built on the first-generation AWS Graviton architecture, the system provides direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, supported by 5 Gbps baseline network performance and hardware AES support. Benchmark results highlight solid parallel efficiency, including 8.6 million Redis SET operations per second and average multi-threaded stress-ng throughput of 24102.93, alongside high cached memory bandwidth of 572.2 GB/sec. However, performance is limited in single-core tasks (418.0 Geekbench single-core) and uncached memory writes (10.05 GB/sec). With no attached local storage or GPU hardware, a1.metal is best suited for scale-out Arm native microservices, static web serving, containerized environments, and light database workloads.
